cards.issue_title: Standardized-view section does not show the product as one market view
summary_4_lines: On the homepage dark block that says the whole market now sits in one standardized view, they could not see that view as a product.
They skipped the video, asked what the block even is, and rejected a plus-button or Excel-sheet overlay as too complex.
They then tabled the section instead of adding graphics.
This is the homepage unique-point copy, not a separate product page.
cards.pinpoint: At about 00:09–01:35 they were on that dark unique-point block; they said the standardized-view claim is something you have to see in the product itself, the current block does not show it, and extra graphics (plus button / Excel background) would be too complex, so they stopped discussing the section.
cards.on_screen_object: Homepage dark region 'We completely re-engineered your home loan journey' and the paragraph 'Now, the entire market sits in one standardized view…'
quotes_sample: Oh no, why are you making it so complex?
Actually, let's not talk about this section.
related_discussion_one_liners: Analogized how a product looks when it is given in the starting.
Already watching the video, so they should not have to tell the one-view line.
Do not want to be scammed; other sites' visuals exist; do not want clicking.
Paid more attention to wording than graphics; wordings can be written immediately.
"It can be cancelled" / "same problem" sat on this visual, not a second defect; later mapped accordion "Every bank's home loan in the same layout" back to this standardized-view point (issue 02).
cards.distinct_from_other_files_in_this_folder: This is the dark unique-point block claiming one standardized view without showing that view as a product, not later sections repeating unique points, not help-strip spacing, and not footer-as-ignored-legal.

cards.issue_title: Later homepage unique-point sections repeat earlier points and bury a seventh
summary_4_lines: After the dark unique-point blocks, Built around you, Scattered everywhere, and the other dark screens say the same six points again.
They treated "Help toward what you need" as a new seventh point whose sentence they could not parse.
They said to scrap Scattered everywhere as a section, keep only useful words, and rebuild the four dark sections so seven points flow in few polished words.
This is homepage information architecture, not a separate bug in one accordion click.
cards.pinpoint: From about 01:36 they clicked through Built around you, mapped four items back to unique points already covered, named Help toward what you need as a seventh unclear point, then said to scrap Scattered everywhere and refactor the four dark sections into a coherent seven-point story with very few words.
cards.on_screen_object: Built around you accordion (#home-built-trigger-0..4), Scattered everywhere. Consolidated here. video section, and the four dark unique-point sections
quotes_sample: I think this is the seventh unique point that we want to convey.
So this sentence what does it mean?
Let's scrap this section as well.
related_discussion_one_liners: Mapped accordion rows to earlier claims: we bring everything to you; every bank's loan the same way → standardized view; browse before number; one application; you can do it yourself or ask us but you still choose.
Liked the Help line as a feeling ("It's nice." "It makes you dance.") without knowing what the sentence meant.
"scattered" / "consolidated" might be reusable words but "we don't want to get carried away" and "We are not writing an essay."
Standardization / scatterization / consolidation was a warning against essay-like copy, not a third issue.
Play/Pause on the Scattered video was inspection, not a player bug.
cards.distinct_from_other_files_in_this_folder: This is later homepage blocks restating unique points and burying an unclear seventh (Help toward what you need), not the missing product visual on the standardized-view block, not help-strip padding, and not footer legal-fit.

cards.issue_title: Get-help strip sits in a padded gap instead of on the footer
summary_4_lines: The peach "Need some help? Chat now or call…" bar is a short strip, but it sits in a large empty gap above the footer.
They measured that gap in the inspector as 52px above and 64px below and called the orange margin overlay the thing to fix.
They said this must not be its own full-screen section; it should sit on the footer on every page, with no extra padding.
They also said help belongs with Support in the nav, not as a seventh story block.
cards.pinpoint: From about 05:14 they called this strip too big because of padding above and below; inspector showed margin 52px 0 64px as orange overlay; they said stick the strip to the footer with no padding, on every page, and do not treat it as an independent full-screen section.
cards.on_screen_object: aside.site-help-strip (Need some help? Chat now / call); complementary landmark Get help
quotes_sample: this padding above it, padding below it is causing some issues
It needs to be fixed to the footer.
related_discussion_one_liners: Earlier holes/stuck-to-footer talk was about a previous version of this strip.
"This footer has a big heat strip" — ASR heat/help; on-screen it is the help strip, not a heat map.
"these two will fly away" / "put on the navel" / "Navel has support" — join to nav Support (dropdown already labeled Support), not a literal navel.
"It is just for some help." They contrasted full-screen sections (occupy whole screen, then scroll) with this mini strip.
Checking the footer immediately after is the handoff to issue 04, not a second help-strip defect.
cards.distinct_from_other_files_in_this_folder: This is the Need-some-help strip's 52px/64px margin making it a padded mini-section instead of sitting on the footer, not unique-point copy or duplication, and not treating the footer itself as an ignored legal block.

cards.issue_title: Footer is treated as a nobody-cares legal block that may not fit
summary_4_lines: After the help strip they looked at the footer itself: columns, disclaimer line, and "Read the full disclaimer."
They said footer UI is not something anyone cares about, it is not a disclaimer, and anything important has to live somewhere else.
They still called the legal/compliance lines okay as legal stuff, then asked whether the footer fits the site from their own perspective — one said it should not, the other said it does.
That "does it fit" question is unfinished here and continues in the next recording on the disclaimer language.
cards.pinpoint: From about 08:12 they inspected the homepage footer, said footer UI is not a disclaimer and no one cares, said important content must be shown elsewhere, then asked whether the footer fits from their perspective (it should not / yes it does) while the disclaimer summary stayed on screen.
cards.on_screen_object: footer.site-footer, p.site-footer-disclaimer-summary, details.site-footer-disclaimer-more (Read the full disclaimer)
related_discussion_one_liners: "Okay, home page is done." / "No, check the footer now."
Help-strip placement (issue 03) is adjacent but they had already finished that when they switched to footer UI.
"Everyone knows this is just legal stuff" is their own framing of why a footer might be ignored, not a separate defect.
cards.distinct_from_other_files_in_this_folder: This is treating the footer UI and disclaimer as a nobody-cares legal dump that may not fit the site, not the help strip's gap above the footer and not homepage unique-point visuals or duplication.
